en: The Complete Ritual for the Bestowal of the Three Stages of the Great Ordination (Mahā-śīla-dharma-vidhi) Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fazang of Beichansi Temple during the Tiantqi Era of the Ming Dynasty Edited and Verified by the Bhikṣu Chaoyuan of Panlong Chan Temple in the Pure Zhongnan Mountains

The Method for Bestowing the Ten Precepts of a Śrāmaṇera, Volume One. (When the attendants have finished arranging the seats, they strike the *qing* three times and follow with the *shu* bell. The Abbot passes the incense; the assembly gathers together. Again, the incense burner is passed to the seat. After the attendant has completed his prostrations, the drum and bells are struck rapidly.

The Preceptor leads the novices to the front of the Abbot’s quarters. They kneel long and join their palms. The Preceptor enters the door, performs one prostration before the ritual implements, stands up and stands to the side. He calls to the novices, saying: "Perform one prostration. They rise and again inquire after his well-being. Finally, he walks forward. The Abbot speaks.)

Homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha (the assembly chants this together). [The Master] is welcomed to the front of the Dharma Hall. The disciples kneel in long prostration with palms joined on both sides. The Upādhyāya either circumambulates the altar.

Having finished the prostrations, he ascends the seat. To provide instruction, he strikes the chime once. The bells and drums fall silent. To provide instruction on the ultimate direction, he performs three full prostrations, then kneels long with palms joined. The Master asks:

"Is the Sangha assembled? (The respondent replies: "It is assembled. (The Master says: "Are you in harmony? (The respondent replies: "We are in harmony. (The Master says: "The Sangha is now in harmony; what is it that you intend to do? (The respondent replies:

"To shave the heads of the sons of the Buddhas and confer the precepts upon them. (The Master says: "Excellent; so be it. (The respondent replies: "Yes. (He withdraws his implements and rises, bows to inquire after [the Master's well-being], and stands to one side.

He calls to the leader, saying: "Offer incense. (Again he says: "All rise together and form a line facing upward. (Upon hearing the sound of the chime, they perform three prostrations with full sincerity, kneel long, and join their palms. The Preceptor leads the recitation of the incense praise.)
By Your Majesty’s grace, I have received ordination; I shall not disobey my parents’ command. Having severed the bonds of affection, I enter the state of non-action (*asaṃskṛta*).
Receiving the ritual and majestic tonsure according to the Master’s Dharma, I don the robes, accept the precepts, and take refuge within my own mind.
Ascending to the First Bhūmi, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas (three times). [Addressing and summoning the sons: "Prostrate three times. [Again:
"O virtuous sons, request the words of the Master; you ought to speak for yourselves.
If you are unable, all follow my lead" (chant and recite as follows):
"Virtuous One, please attend to me with one mind. I, [Name], now request the Virtuous One to serve as my Preceptor for Tonsure and Ordination.
May the Virtuous One act as my Preceptor for Tonsure and Ordination. By relying upon the Virtuous One, I shall obtain the Dharma of tonsure and ordination.
Out of compassion (one prostration). Out of compassion (one prostration). Out of great compassion (one prostration). (The Master strikes the sounding block.)
"O sons of noble family, since you have so earnestly extended this request, I shall act as your preceptor for the tonsure and the conferral of the precepts.
Listen attentively to all that I shall reveal. (Again, he strikes the sounding block: "O sons of the Buddha, this single Dharma is the source of the mind, profoundly still and tranquil;
it is a sea of Dharma, deep and vast. Those who are deluded by it will sink and drift for eternal kalpas; those who awaken to it shall attain liberation right where they stand."
Liberated. Those who seek to return to the Way find no path superior to leaving the household life. It is as expansive as space; its purity is like the bright moon.

When the conditions for practice are complete, the fruit of the Way is not far off. Beginning with the merit of moment-to-moment mindfulness, one ultimately realizes the stage of non-action (*asaṃskṛta*).
Therefore, our Great Awakened World-Honored One renounced the precious throne of the Golden Wheel, scaled the city walls at midnight, and cast off his finery.
Clad in dragon-patterned robes, with hair cropped short upon the green mountains, they allow magpies’ nests to rest atop their heads and spiderwebs to hang between their brows.

By cultivating quiescence, they realize the eternal truth; by severing worldly toil, they achieve perfect enlightenment. Among the Buddhas of the three periods, none have spoken of attaining the Way while remaining a householder.
Among the patriarchs of successive generations, who has ever practiced defilement to save others? Therefore, from Buddha to Buddha, there has been a transmission of the Dharma.

Transmitted from patriarch to patriarch, remaining untainted by worldly conditions, one only then becomes a vessel for the Dharma. Thus, celestial Māras fold their hands in submission and non-Buddhists turn their hearts toward the Way.
Above, they repay the fourfold debt of gratitude; below, they rescue sentient beings from suffering. Therefore it is said:
"While wandering within the three realms, one cannot abandon love and affection. To cast aside such affection and enter the unconditioned—this is truly the repayment of gratitude. O virtuous sons...
"Children, the dharma of renunciation transcends ordinary worldly sentiments. One does not bow to kings, nor does one bow to parents. You may now leave these seats;
with focused devotion, pay your respects and take your leave, mindful of the King’s grace in providing this land and water, and your parents’ virtue in giving you life.
Hereafter, do not bow. (He exhorted his sons, saying: "Perform one prostration. Rising, inquire after their well-being. Turn away. The Preceptor then raised his voice:)
I now take my leave of the King to become a śramaṇa under the Buddha. I vow to attain the Unsurpassed Way in order to repay the King’s kindness.
(The disciples join in harmony; each disciple bows once for every line. When finished, they inquire after his well-being. The Upādhyāya says:)
"I now take leave of my parents to become a śramaṇa under the Buddha. May I propagate the unsurpassed Way to repay the kindness of my parents.
(As before, after the prostrations are completed, the instructor says: "Rise and inquire after his well-being; turn around, kneel long, and join your palms. (The Upādhyāya says:)
"O sons of noble family, you have already taken leave of the king and your parents.

I, with the pure Dharma-water of the Tathāgata, shall appoint a karma-ācārya to pour water upon the crowns of your heads, thereby purifying your bodies and minds and eliminating all demonic obstacles."
Born from the Buddha’s own mouth, transformed by birth through the Dharma, you are the sons of the Dharma King; you should feel great joy. (He opens the way and summons the sons, who reply:
"We pray only that you will, out of compassion and pity, take us under your care. (The sons prostrate once. The Master takes the pure flask and hands it to the Karma Master, speaking again:)
"O sons of noble family, this final knot is called the *cūḍā*. Only the Master alone is able to sever it.
With the adamantine blade of Tathāgata-wisdom, I shall appoint an instructor-ācārya to remove it for you, so that you may perfectly achieve the marks of a monk.

You should feel great joy. (He then exhorted and summoned the sons, who replied: "We pray only that you will look upon us with compassion and pity, and grant us your guidance and protection. (The sons prostrated.)

First, the Master raises the razor and instructs the student. Second, the Ācārya emerges from the assembly to confer the empowerment and shave the head. The Master says: "Excellent, true son of the Buddha!
By touching your crown, you are certified to non-arising. Now you receive the prediction of Bodhi; in the future, the fruit shall be spontaneously realized."
(He led the assembly in chanting, joining in with every line. The Master then raised his voice again:
"Excellent, great man! You are able to realize the impermanence of the world. Shaving your hair to hasten toward Nirvana—this is rare and inconceivable."
(The assembly joins in harmony as before. The Master again raises his voice:

Altering one's appearance to maintain the will and integrity, severing affection to bid farewell to kin; leaving the household life to propagate the holy Way, demonstrating the means to deliver all sentient beings.

(2. The Acharya: After the consecration and shaving of the head are completed, he bows to inquire after [the master’s] well-being and returns to his place. He receives the assembly as before. To provide guidance, he calls out: "Perform three prostrations. The Master says:)

"O śrāmaṇeras, since you have already undergone tonsure and ordination, I shall now bestow upon you the alms bowl, the three robes, and the requisites. (The preceptor performs the empowerment; the śrāmaṇera should receive it.)
The Master said:
"The *pātra* is a vessel of standard measure for daily use; it is now conferred for you to hold.
The *antarvāsaka*, a five-strip robe, is conferred—one long strip and one short strip."

"Venerable sir, please attend to me with one-pointed mind. I, the śrāmaṇera [Name], now receive this *uttarāsaṅga*—a seven-strip robe consisting of two long and one short pieces of cut cloth—and maintain it.
I now receive this *saṃghāṭī*—a twenty-five-strip robe consisting of four long and one short pieces—and maintain it.
I now receive this *niṣīdana*, made according to the prescribed measurements, and maintain it. (Each of these items is to be presented by the preceptor and received by the disciple.)
When the transmission of the bowl is complete, the instructor calls the *śrāmaṇera* forward, saying: "Arise, stand by my side, and hang the bowl.

The Master recites the verse: "The *pātra* is a vessel of proper measure; Because it is used daily, I now transmit its holding. (Once the hanging is finished, he stops speaking. The instructor calls the various disciples forward, saying: "Kneel upright and join your palms."
The Master further consecrates the robes and requisites (the ritual for the transformation and prohibition is the same as before):
"Excellent are the five robes, the garments of liberation; the supreme field of merit. I now receive them upon my head, never to be parted from them in life after life."
Oṃ siddhaye svāhā. Sevenfold robe, most excellent, garment of liberation;
supreme field of merit, I now receive you upon my head, that in every birth I may always wear you.
Oṃ dhupe dhupe svāhā. Great robe, well-spoken,
garment of liberation, supreme field of merit— fulfilling the command of the Tathāgata, may you widely deliver all deluded beings.
Oṃ mahākāpota-siddhi svāhā. Seat and bedding, the *niṣīdana*.
Nourishing the sprout of the mind-nature, unfolding to ascend to the ground of the sages, one carries out the command of the Tathāgata.
Oṃ damba damba svāhā. (The assembly likewise repeats this mantra, chanting in unison with the voice and bowing as they finish. The Master says: "Virtuous sons, the Dharma is like a great ocean;

one enters it gradually and becomes increasingly deep. Since you have left the household life, you must first receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts before you may become a lay follower (*upāsaka*) close to the Great Sangha.
Next, you shall receive the Ten Precepts of a *śrāmaṇera*, whereupon you may truly be considered members of the Sangha."
Regarding material gain, the matter lies in single-minded sincerity; you must not harbor thoughts of arrogance.

I now, for your sake, with a single heart, reverently entreat the Triple Gem and the various devas who protect the Dharma to provide guidance, support, and protection, so that you may be worthy of receiving the precepts.
You should look up with longing, be diligent and reverent, and surrender yourself to me as I single-mindedly and sincerely offer this invocation. (The instructor says:)
The Invocation with Incense and Flowers (alternatively: The Request with Incense and Flowers). [The Master says:
I, [Name], with single-minded devotion, respectfully invite the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Pure Dharma-body of the Flower Treasury World; the World-Honored One Rocana, the Perfect Reward-body;
and the World-Honored One Śākyamuni, our Original Teacher, who manifests in hundreds of thousands of millions of transformation-bodies, and who provides guidance from the Western Paradise.
World-Honored One Amitābha; World-Honored One Maitreya, who will descend in the future; and all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive Dharma-realm:
we pray that you do not violate your original vows, but rather gather us with your compassionate light to bear witness to our receiving of the precepts.
(The Master says: "Perform three prostrations. (He further says: "The incense and flowers lead the way.
(He further says: "The incense and flowers invite [the Dharma]. (The Master says:

"I, [Name], with single-minded devotion, respectfully invite the Vinaya-piṭaka of the Great and Small Vehicles, the five sections and three clusters, the liberation and the Prātimokṣa, and the twelve divisions of the Tripiṭaka."
The scriptures that distinguish between the provisional and the ultimate, the true, pure, and profound Dharma-treasure: Homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* of the Great Vaipulya.
With single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay respectful homage. (The officiant says: "Perform three prostrations. He speaks again:)
The Invocation with Incense and Flowers (also known as the Request with Incense and Flowers). [The Master says:

"I, [Name], with single-minded devotion, respectfully invite Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, the youth Sudhana, the Dragon Girl and her true lords, and the oceanic assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra."
To all the great Bodhisattvas; to the Venerable Upāli at the assembly of the Vinaya Piṭaka; to the successive patriarchs of India and China;
to the various great Vinaya masters of Mount Zhongnan; to the Great Monk Bai of the Upper and Lower Qingquan Halls on Mount Hui;
to the Great Monk Jian of the Upper and Lower Longchang Halls on Mount Hua; and to the Huayan Hall of Mount Fu.
To the late Great Master (Dharma Seal) Wenxiao, the founding patriarch of this monastery and the venerable monks of successive generations, as well as to the two Chan Masters Zhoubo and Mingzhi:
we pray that you will not forsake your original vows, but extend your compassionate light to encompass us, and bear witness to our receiving of the precepts.
(The Ritual Master says: "Perform three prostrations with full obeisance. (He further says:

"Incense and flowers lead the way" (alternatively: "Incense and flowers invite"). (The Master says: "I, [Name], with single-minded devotion, respectfully invite all the devas of various stations from the assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*:
Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others, and the virtuous deities who protect the precepts."
Vajrapāṇi, the great deities and spirits of the mountains, rivers, the great earth, water, land, and space, and all the true lords of the monasteries and the local soil:
we pray that you do not violate your original vows, but descend upon this ordination platform and provide diligent, solemn protection.

(The Master says: "All you sons of noble family, the Three Jewels are present and the myriad deities stand guard. If you wish to seek the precepts of refuge, you must first purify yourselves of transgressions and flaws.
It is like washing a garment before applying dye. Now, with utmost sincerity, follow me in repentance. (He raises his voice: "Recite!"
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion, Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent for it all.
(Recite each line with a prostration as appropriate; then the Master says:)
"O sons of good family, since you have now purified the actions of body, speech, and mind, you should take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
(The Master says: "I [Name] take refuge in the Buddha; I take refuge in the Dharma; I take refuge in the Saṅgha."
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire; I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the Honored One among assemblies.
Having completed taking refuge in the Buddha, having completed taking refuge in the Dharma, having completed taking refuge in the Saṅgha.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is my World-Honored One; I now take refuge in him out of compassion (one prostration).
Out of compassion (one prostration). Out of great compassion (the above; the Master recites three times, the disciple responds three times. When finished, three prostrations. The Master says:)

"O sons of noble family, since you have already abandoned the heterodox and returned to the orthodox, and your precepts are now fully perfected, if you wish to recognize the characteristics [of the precepts] and maintain them, I shall confer the five precepts upon you. (The Master says: "I, [Name]..."
Not killing, not stealing, and for as long as life lasts not engaging in sexual misconduct—these are the fundamental precepts. Are you able to uphold them? (The answer is: I am able to uphold them.
No false speech; no drinking of intoxicants. (The Master strikes the sounding block and says:
"O sons of good family, regarding these five precepts, you must not violate even a single one. Are you able to uphold them? (They reply: "We are able."
The Preceptor (instructing the novice to enter, says): "Perform three prostrations. The Preceptor (further says): "Those who receive the five precepts, rise and exit" (the Master says).
"O sons of good family, the five precepts are the primary cause for entering the Path and the foremost means of escaping the three miserable realms.

I shall now confer upon you the ten śrāmaṇera precepts, whereby your physical form will be fully endowed with the dharma-rituals; this is called 'the diligent one' (śikṣamāṇa). You shall dwell under the guidance of a teacher and receive benefits equal to those of the monastic community;
such is the śrāmaṇera who accords with the Dharma. You should receive this with the highest reverence. (The Teacher says: "I, [Name]..."
Not killing living beings;
not stealing; not engaging in sexual misconduct.
Not speaking falsely, not engaging in frivolous speech, not using double-tongued speech, and not using harsh speech;
and not drinking intoxicants for as long as life lasts—can you uphold these śrāmaṇera precepts? (He answers: I can uphold them.
He does not wear fragrant garlands or apply perfumes to his body;
he does not engage in singing, dancing, or theatrical performances, nor does he go to watch or listen to them;
he does not sit on high, wide, or large beds.
"Not eating at improper times;

not grasping or holding raw gold, silver, or precious objects—from abstaining from taking life up to not grasping or holding raw gold, silver, or precious objects—are you able to observe these? (He replies: "I am able to observe them."
(The Master said: "These ten precepts of this branch must not be transgressed one by one. Are you able to uphold them? (The candidate replied: "I am able to uphold them. (The Master said:
"O sons of good family, after you have now received these precepts, you must receive them upon the crown of your head and maintain them faithfully.

You must not violate the precepts you have undertaken. Make offerings to the Triple Gem, diligently cultivate fields of merit, and toward your Upādhyāya and Ācārya, act exactly according to the Dharma."
The Teaching: Toward those of superior, middling, and inferior status, one should always maintain a mind of reverence. Practice the Path with diligent effort to repay the kindness of one’s parents.
As for clothing, take only what covers the body, not for its ornamental patterns; as for food, take only what sustains life, not for the sake of indulging in flavors.

Let flowers, perfumes, and cosmetics never come near the person. Regarding beautiful forms and improper sounds, do not look or listen at all. Speak slowly and maintain rectitude; do not proclaim the faults of others. Should there be...

As for "contention": when two doctrines harmonize, there is distinction between male and female, yet no injury to grasses or trees. One does not befriend those who are not virtuous, nor does one take as a master those who are not sages.
Dharma-robes and alms-bowls are always kept with one; one does not eat at improper times and does not speak what is not in accordance with the Dharma.

Diligently contemplating the meaning, one reviews the old to know the new. When seated, one practices meditative reflection; when rising, one recites and chants. Thus, the three evil paths are closed and Nirvana is opened.
Entering the gates of the Dharma, within the discipline of the bhikṣus, one increases right action, never regresses from the bodhicitta, and maintains the perpetual illumination of prajñā-wisdom.
Widely transforming sentient beings so that they all equally attain perfect enlightenment—truly a disciple of the Buddha whose application of mind is such as this.
(The Master strikes the sounding block and says:
"O sons of noble family, from this moment until you descend from the altar, diligently cultivate precept, concentration, and wisdom, and extinguish greed, anger, and delusion.
Furthermore, you shall receive the śrāmaṇera precepts on such-and-such a year, month, day, and hour. Once this sacred rite is completed, you shall be born [into the noble lineage]."
"Thankful Joy. One bows, rises, and performs the ritual of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*). (The Instructor says: "Perform one bow, rise, and [the Master] raises [his voice] to say...")
The supreme practice of the merit of receiving the precepts—may all boundless and excellent blessings be dedicated.

May all sentient beings submerged in suffering swiftly proceed to the immeasurable and vast Buddha-fields. Through the causes and conditions of this dedication, may the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the various Honored Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and the Mahāprajñāpāramitā [be honored].

(The Instructor says: "There is no need to rise from your seats. With utmost sincerity, prostrate to the Abbot and the various masters. After three prostrations, rise from your seats and inquire after their well-being. (He speaks again: "Form the ranks. (He speaks again: "At the end, proceed forward. (When the bells and drums sound together, the Master raises [the incense burner]).
*Namo* to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha.

(Proceeding to the front of the abbot’s quarters, the *kaidō* calls to the śrāmaṇeras: "Kneel long with palms joined. Wait for the Master to enter the room. Once he has entered, the *kaidō* performs three prostrations, rises, and stands by his side. He calls to the śrāmaṇeras: 'Perform one prostration, rise, and inquire after his well-being.
He speaks again: 'Form ranks; those at the end of the line go forward first. The bells and drums cease simultaneously.')

The Middle Volume of the Exposition of the Bhikṣu Precepts (*Bhikṣu-śīla-dharma*) [When the attendants have finished arranging the seats, the *qing* gong is struck three times. The Chan Hall opens for the Great Silence (*da-jing*). The bell is struck, and the Abbot’s quarters transmits the incense. The assembly gathers together. The attendant transmits the incense burner to the seat of honor. After the prostrations are completed, the Instructor rolls the hand-bell. The Hall Master beats the drum. He then summons the novices (*śrāmaṇera*), who take their positions at the rear.

They proceed forward to the place of the Nine Masters. The novices stand facing each other on both sides. The Instructor turns toward the Nine Masters, performs a single prostration with his ritual implements (*chujù*) touching the ground, and stands to the side. He summons the novices, saying: "Form ranks upward."]

Having performed one prostration, they inquire after his well-being and divide into ranks. It is further said that at the end, the *kaidō* (the instructor) goes forward first. Upon reaching the front of the abbot’s quarters (*jōbō*), he turns, kneels for a long time with palms joined, and stands waiting outside the door while the nine masters turn to stand by his side.

He waits for the *karmadāna* (ceremonial master) to arrive; once he has taken his place in the center, all the masters together perform one prostration toward the upper direction and each returns to their original position. The *kaidō* spreads out his sitting mat (*gu*), performs three prostrations, and rises to stand by the side.

He calls to the *śrāmaṇeras*, saying: "All rise together and form a line facing upward. They spread out half-mats (*hangu*) and perform three prostrations. Having inquired after his well-being, they kneel for a long time with palms joined. The *kaidō* then speaks.
"O sons of good family, each of you shall record the name of your preceptor for receiving the precepts, as well as the names of the nine teachers;
do not let them be forgotten. (Then he says:)
First: Master [Name] of [Place], acting as the Upādhyāya for the conferral of the precepts for all of you.
Second: Chan Master [Name] of [Place], acting as the Karmācārya for all of you.
In the third position is Chan Master [Name] of [Place], who serves as the *upādhyāya* (preceptor) for instruction for you all.
In the fourth position is Chan Master [Name] of [Place], who serves as the *karmavācanācārya* (witnessing preceptor) for you all.
In the fifth position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For all of you, he serves as the Honored Witness Acharya.
In the sixth position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For all of you, he serves as the Honored Witness Acharya.
In the seventh position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For you all, he shall serve as the Honored Witness Ācārya.
In the eighth position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For you all, he shall serve as the Honored Witness Ācārya.
In the ninth position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For all of you, he serves as the Honored Witness Ācārya.
In the tenth position: Chan Master [Name] of [Place]. For all of you, he serves as the Honored Witness Ācārya.
(The Instructor calls to the śrāmaṇeras: "With utmost sincerity, perform three prostrations.
The Instructor makes the following announcement: "A bright mirror on its stand reflects whatever form it encounters; a great bell on its frame resounds whenever it is struck.

To fulfill the three categories of precepts, one must rely upon the three masters; to examine and rectify the seven transgressions, one entirely depends upon the seven witnesses. Now, for your sake, we shall invite the presiding [monks]..."
The preceptors who previously served as your *karmācārya*, *śikṣācārya*, and *pratyakṣācārya*:
all their words of invitation shall follow my lead (I shall provide the guidance and recite in Sanskrit; the śrāmaṇera shall respond in harmony).
"Venerable One, please attend to me with a single mind. I, [Name], now request the Venerable One to serve as my *karmavācanā*-instructor and witness-ācārya.
May the Venerable One act as my *karmavācanā*-instructor and witness-ācārya.

By relying upon the Venerable One, I shall receive the full ordination (*upasampadā*). Out of compassion (one prostration). Out of compassion (one prostration). Out of great compassion (one prostration)."
(The Karmācārya says: "O sons of the Buddha!
Since you have made this earnest request, I, as the Karmācārya, the Śikṣācārya, and the Upādhyāya before you, shall act for you. Be pure; do not be negligent. (Śrāmaṇera...)
[The Master] replies: "I shall receive this upon my head and carry it out. [He then] instructs and summons the novices, saying: "Perform one prostration. [He] speaks again:
"Now, on your behalf, I have invited the master of such-and-such a school from such-and-such a place to serve as your Preceptor for Receiving the Precepts (Upādhyāya).
All words that follow shall be spoken by me; [the instructor] recites in Sanskrit, and the śrāmaṇeras respond in harmony."
"Venerable One, please attend for a moment. I, [Name], now request the Venerable One to serve as my Preceptor for the Attainment of Full Ordination (*upasampadā*).
May the Venerable One serve as my Preceptor for the Attainment of Full Ordination. Relying upon the Venerable One, I shall receive the full ordination.
Out of compassion, [one prostration]. Out of compassion, [one prostration]. Out of great compassion, [one prostration] (the Preceptor strikes the sounding-block)."
"O sons of the Buddha, since you have all so earnestly extended this request, I shall act as your Upādhyāya for the attainment of the precepts.

Be pure and do not be negligent. (The śrāmaṇeras respond: "We receive and practice this with reverence. (The Preceptor calls to the śrāmaṇeras: "Perform one prostration. Rise, inquire after my well-being, and divide into ranks.
(He further says: "At the end, proceed first. (The Upādhyāya raises [his hand]).
*Namo to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha* (The assembly joins in harmony. They are welcomed to the front of the Dharma Hall. The śrāmaṇera turns to face them, kneels long with palms joined.

The ten masters enter the Dharma Hall, circumambulate the altar once, and then proceed to the second level, standing solemnly facing upward. The ritual attendant strikes the *qing* three times; the bells and drums temporarily cease. Next, the ten masters perform three full prostrations, then kneel long with palms joined. The Kaodaō takes his place before them and recites the text for the Longevity of the Emperor).
It is solely the planting of the seed of Bodhi; it looks to the precepts and discipline as its roots; it is truly the embankment of the True Dharma;
and it serves forever as the moat and rampart of the Citadel of the Mind. Without relying on external protection, how could its widespread transmission be made secure?

(The *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya-śāstra* states: "Whenever one wishes to receive the precepts, one should first expound the Dharma to them, guiding and instructing them so that they give rise to a mind of compassion toward all objects; thus, they shall attain the superior precepts. The *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya-śāstra* states: "Whenever one wishes to receive the precepts, one must first preach the Dharma for you to guide and enlighten you:

'O you people, since beginningless time, you have committed various evil karmas upon all objects; these evils pervade the entire dharma-realm. Now, wishing to receive the precepts, you must overturn those former evil objects.'"
Because they simultaneously give rise to wholesome minds, the precepts are the cause by which [the merit] returns to pervade the entire Dharma-realm.

Therefore, I, the Tathāgata, in accordance with the minds of sentient beings, perform boundless deeds and establish boundless precepts. Since the precepts follow what is established, they must take objects as their conditions.
Although the measure of these objects is vast, to state the essentials, they do not exceed two kinds: first, the realm of sentient beings; second, the realm of non-sentient things.

Regarding "objects" (*viṣaya*): as for what is called the "sentient aspect of objects," from the Buddhas above down to sentient beings below—the primary retributions (*pratyātmika-vipāka*) of the ten realms, as well as sentient beings in the intermediate state (*antarābhava*)—all those who possess mind are termed "sentient objects.
As for "non-sentient objects," these are the environmental retributions (*bhājana-loka*) of the ten realms:
all things in the world such as mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, and forests; boats, carts, houses, dwellings, fields, and gardens; and earth, water, fire, wind, and space.
"Emptiness, consciousness, and so forth—these are the teachings spoken by the Buddha. Confucian texts, images, stupas, temples, and the like, are termed non-sentient objects.
O sons of the Buddha, since you now know that these objects are so vast and expansive, you must rely upon them to give rise to the resolve for enlightenment (bodhicitta).
There are three grades of this mind; the middle and lower grades are weak and inferior, capable only of saving oneself but unable to save others. I shall now instruct you..."
You have generated the supreme mind and seek the supreme precepts. What constitutes the supreme mind?
It is now, before me and in the presence of all my teachers, that you establish three vows: first, the vow to sever all evil, such that there is no evil left unsevered;
second, the vow to cultivate all goodness, such that there is no goodness left uncultivated; third, the vow to deliver all sentient beings, such that not a single sentient being is left behind.

He does not cross over [to the other shore]. Having made these three kinds of great vows, at the conclusion of the formal ritual of the *jñapti-caturtha-karman*, he proceeds to confer the full *bhikṣu* precepts.

This is not merely for the sake of seeking the minor fruits of the *śrāvaka*, but because he directly desires to accomplish the Threefold Pure Precepts (*tri-koṭi-śīla*), to advance toward the three gates of liberation (*trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni*), and to correctly seek the fruit of Buddhahood and Great Nirvāṇa so that the Dharma may long endure. Thus he makes his resolve.

You must instead cultivate a body with a capacity like that of empty space; only then will you be able [to receive them].
